events.title: Italian port workers hold 24 hour national strike
events.severity_basis: A single 24 hour stoppage with partial participation; the PSA Pra' terminal at Genoa was reported fully stopped for the day, a single terminal affected for under 72 hours.
events.summary: Port workers across Italy stopped work for 24 hours on 2026-09-28 (28 September 2026) in a national strike called by the USB Mare e Porti union, with the Orsa ports union joining at Gioia Tauro. The union asked the government to recognise port work as arduous for pension purposes and opposed the wider use of temporary agency labour. Terminals at Genoa, Livorno, Gioia Tauro and Civitavecchia warned customers of possible delays to vessels, gates and cargo handling. The union said the PSA Pra' terminal at Genoa stood completely still and that participation exceeded 50 percent at several other ports. Those figures come from the union and were not independently confirmed. La Spezia was not on strike, and the union said it would continue its national mobilisation.

timeline.text: USB Mare e Porti announces a national port strike for 28 September and a demonstration outside the Genoa prefecture over the recognition of port work as arduous.

The 24 hour strike runs from 00:01 to midnight. Terminals including PSA SECH, PSA Genova Pra' and Terminal Darsena Toscana warn that normal operations cannot be guaranteed, and demonstrations are held at Genoa, Gioia Tauro and Civitavecchia.

The union reports the PSA Pra' terminal fully stopped, over 70 percent participation at other Genoa terminals and at Gioia Tauro, and over 60 percent at the Livorno container terminals, and says it will continue its mobilisation.

cause.text: The union called the strike to demand recognition of port work as arduous for pension purposes, a government committee it says was promised in May and not convened, and to oppose amendments widening temporary agency labour in ports.
cause.attributed_by: USB Mare e Porti and Or.S.A. Mari e Porti, as reported

resolution.text: The stoppage ended at midnight as scheduled. The union said it would continue and strengthen its national mobilisation, and no agreement with the government was reported.

events.no_effect_note: Our port call series end on 2026-09-25, before the strike, and a single day stoppage with partial participation is unlikely to stand out in daily port calls at these ports.

events.title: Hurricane Polo restricts shipping at Mexican Pacific ports
events.severity_basis: Lazaro Cardenas was reported closed to larger vessels from 2026-09-22 to 2026-09-25 and our portwatch-port-calls series shows zero calls there on 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24, a port wide stoppage of 24 hours to 7 days; Manzanillo stayed open to large ships.
events.summary: Hurricane Polo, which reached Category 5 strength offshore of southwestern Mexico on 2026-09-22 (22 September 2026), led the Mexican Navy to restrict navigation at several Pacific ports. Acapulco and Zihuatanejo were closed to all vessels, while Manzanillo, Lazaro Cardenas, Puerto Marques and Puerto Escondido were closed to smaller vessels or, in one report, larger ones at Lazaro Cardenas. Manzanillo, the country's largest container port, kept handling large ships. Zihuatanejo reopened on 2026-09-25 after three days, and Lazaro Cardenas reopened to larger vessels that afternoon. The storm stayed offshore and did not make landfall in this region, and later closures on the Baja California peninsula are not covered by this record.

timeline.text: As Polo strengthens to Category 5, the Manzanillo Port Captaincy bars vessels under 500 gross tonnage from 9 a.m. while larger ships keep working, and navigation is barred at Acapulco, Zihuatanejo, Puerto Marques and Lazaro Cardenas for smaller craft, with Acapulco and Zihuatanejo closed to larger vessels as well.

The Mexican Navy confirms closures to all vessels at Acapulco and Zihuatanejo and to small vessels at Manzanillo, Lazaro Cardenas and Puerto Escondido, as the hurricane, now Category 4, drifts offshore.
The Zihuatanejo port captaincy lifts the navigation ban after three days.
Lazaro Cardenas reopens from 2 p.m. to larger vessels once waves fall below two metres; smaller craft stay restricted for the time being.

cause.text: The Mexican Navy and port captaincies restricted navigation as a precaution against high winds, heavy rain and large waves from Hurricane Polo as it moved slowly north offshore.
cause.attributed_by: Secretaria de Marina and port captaincies, as reported

resolution.text: Zihuatanejo and Lazaro Cardenas reopened to navigation on 2026-09-25 as sea conditions eased.

events.title: Typhoon Dujuan halts cargo calls at Yokohama and Tokyo Bay ports
events.severity_basis: Measured effects at two or more ports; the portwatch-port-calls series records 3 calls at Yokohama and 2 at Tokyo on 2026-09-20 against daily means of about 36 and 24 over 2026-08-23 to 2026-09-18, with similar falls at Kawasaki and Chiba.
events.summary: Typhoon Dujuan passed close to the Kanto region of Japan on 2026-09-21 (21 September 2026), bringing record rainfall, flooding and landslides. Kuehne+Nagel reports that the Port of Yokohama was closed for 45 hours from 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-22. Our port call series shows Yokohama, Tokyo, Kawasaki and Chiba falling to near zero daily calls on 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-21 and returning to normal levels on 2026-09-22. The closure was followed straight away by national holidays on 2026-09-21 to 2026-09-23, so yards stayed full and vessel waits at Yokohama reached 1.5 to 2 days.

timeline.text: Yokohama closes as the typhoon approaches Tokyo Bay; the closure lasts about 45 hours.
Dujuan passes close to Tokyo and the Kanto region with heavy rain and strong winds; nearly 500 flights are cancelled, trains are suspended and a record 832 mm of rain is recorded.
Yokohama's 45 hour closure ends and port calls at Yokohama, Tokyo, Kawasaki and Chiba return to usual levels, though Kuehne+Nagel reported power outages and rail disruption continuing that day.
Kuehne+Nagel reports Yokohama still recovering, with yard density near 90 percent and vessel waits of 1.5 to 2 days after the holidays.

cause.text: Typhoon Dujuan brought high seas, strong winds and record rainfall to the Kanto coast, and the Port of Yokohama suspended operations for 45 hours.
cause.attributed_by: Logistics firms Kuehne+Nagel and SEKO Logistics, as reported

resolution.text: Port calls at Yokohama, Tokyo, Kawasaki and Chiba returned to normal levels on 2026-09-22, although yard congestion and vessel waiting times stayed elevated for about a further week.

events.title: Typhoon Saudel closes Ningbo and Shanghai container terminals
events.severity_basis: Measured effects at two ports; the portwatch-port-calls series records 0 to 3 calls at Ningbo on 2026-08-26 and 2026-08-27 and 1 call at Shanghai on 2026-08-27, against daily means of about 49 and 88 in the preceding weeks.
events.summary: Typhoon Saudel stopped container handling at Ningbo-Zhoushan and Shanghai in late August 2026, about two weeks after Typhoon Dolphin. Ningbo suspended empty container work from 16:00 on 2026-08-26 (26 August 2026) and all terminal operations that evening, with roughly 800 vessels reported moved to safe anchorages. Yangshan halted on 2026-08-27 (27 August 2026) and Waigaoqiao suspended empty container work the same day. Saudel came ashore in southern Zhejiang around midday on 2026-08-28 (28 August 2026), and terminals at Waigaoqiao, Yangshan and Ningbo reopened between midday and 15:00 that day. Forwarders warned that bunched arrivals would add to congestion already present across North Asia.

timeline.text: Ningbo suspends empty container operations at 16:00 and all container terminal operations by the evening, at its highest typhoon response level.
Shanghai's Yangshan halts operations at 06:00 and Waigaoqiao suspends empty container work; Ningbo yards and warehouses also close.
Saudel makes landfall in southern Zhejiang around midday; Waigaoqiao reopens at 12:00, Yangshan at 14:00 and Ningbo terminals at 15:00.

cause.text: Port operators suspended terminal work under typhoon emergency responses activated by local authorities as the storm approached the Zhejiang and Fujian coast.
cause.attributed_by: Ningbo and Shanghai port authorities and terminal operators, as reported by logistics firms

resolution.text: Terminals in Shanghai and Ningbo reopened between 12:00 and 15:00 on 2026-08-28 as the storm weakened, though berthing delays continued.

events.title: Ver.di warning strikes halt container handling at German seaports
events.severity_basis: Two warning strikes, 24 hours from the night shift of 2026-08-17 and 48 hours from the late shift of 2026-09-02, largely stopped container handling at Hamburg, a port-wide stoppage of 24 hours to 7 days.
organisations: Central Association of German Seaport Operators (ZDS)
events.summary: Workers at six German seaports, Hamburg, Bremerhaven, Wilhelmshaven, Bremen, Emden and Brake, held a 24-hour warning strike from the night shift of 2026-08-17 (17 August 2026), the first in a wage dispute between the ver.di union and the ZDS employers' association covering about 11,000 workers. Eurogate said no cargo could be handled at its Hamburg terminal for the period, and HHLA reported delays at its Hamburg terminals. A second warning strike, lasting 48 hours in Hamburg, began with the late shift on 2026-09-02 (2 September 2026) after members rejected an employer offer. Employers then tabled a 12-month proposal, put to a union consultation running to 2026-09-14, with indefinite action possible if it was rejected. The outcome of that vote was not found at the time of drafting.

timeline.text: Ver.di begins a 24-hour warning strike at six German seaports,, with night shifts at Hamburg, Bremerhaven and Wilhelmshaven stopping work.
Operations at Hamburg's main container terminals are reported largely halted, and inland rail and truck services warn of delays and possible cancellations.
A second, 48-hour warning strike starts with the late shift at Hamburg, Bremerhaven, Bremen, Wilhelmshaven, Emden and Brake after workers rejected an employer offer of 5.1 percent over 18 months.
After a fourth negotiating round, employers offer a 12-month agreement with a 3.4 percent retroactive increase, which ver.di puts to its members in a consultation running until 2026-09-14.

cause.text: The union called warning strikes after wage talks with the seaport employers' association stalled. Ver.di sought an 8.2 percent hourly rise on a 12-month term, and employers had offered 5.1 percent over 18 months.
cause.attributed_by: ver.di and ZDS, as reported by trade press

events.title: Durban Gateway Terminal backlog follows terminal operating system cutover
events.severity_basis: Terminal disruption lasting over 72 hours at a major container terminal; portwatch-port-calls for Durban averaged about 5 calls a week from 2026-08-17 against about 6.7 in June and July.
organisations: Southern African Association of Freight Forwarders
events.summary: Durban Gateway Terminal, a container terminal at Durban, South Africa, began working through a growing backlog after it switched to the Navis N4 terminal operating system on 2026-08-15 (15 August 2026). The operator had told users that vessel and landside work would pause for about twelve hours during the cutover and that some delays would follow. Reports from the following two weeks describe queues of trucks waiting up to about 30 hours, ships waiting longer at anchorage, refrigerated export containers spoiling in queues, and a temporary pause on accepting reefer boxes. The operator said the system was stable by 2026-08-27 but that equipment constraints and yard congestion meant a return to normal would take time.

timeline.text: A freight forwarders association relays the terminal's notice of a cutover to the new operating system, starting 18:00 on 15 August, with no vessel or landside operations for about twelve hours.
The terminal goes live on Navis N4; users must register afresh for access.

Reports describe truck queues of up to about 30 hours, longer vessel stays and spoiled refrigerated cargo. The terminal pauses acceptance of reefer boxes, says the system is stable, and says equipment limits and the backlog mean normal flow will take time.

cause.text: The backlog followed a planned migration to a new terminal operating system, with equipment limits and yard congestion cited as further factors.
cause.attributed_by: Durban Gateway Terminal, as reported

events.title: Earthquake suspends container terminals at Colombia's Buenaventura port
events.severity_basis: Terminal operations were suspended from 2026-08-10 and restarted only in phases from 2026-08-12, with the main inland corridor still impaired on 2026-08-14; this is an editor judgment because no port series covers Buenaventura.
events.summary: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck western Colombia at about 07:34 local time on 2026-08-10 (10 August 2026), with its epicentre near San Jose del Palmar in Choco. Container operations at Buenaventura, Colombia's main Pacific gateway, were suspended while terminals inspected damage, and road closures cut the port off from the interior. Maersk skipped one call and left a vessel part worked. Some operators restarted in stages from 2026-08-12, but by 2026-08-14 yard space was very tight, staff were short and the Cali to Buenaventura corridor was not fully restored. Colombia's Atlantic coast ports were reported unaffected. No recovery date had been reported by the last source retrieved.

timeline.text: The earthquake strikes, APM Terminals Buenaventura activates its emergency protocols and evacuates precautionarily, and container terminal operations are suspended.
Maersk reports terminal operations suspended pending assessments, a vessel unable to finish cargo work and a skipped call, while road closures disrupt cargo to and from the interior.
Terminal operators begin phased restarts, with the SPRBUN terminal handling container ships and ro-ro vessels after engineering inspections and APM Terminals reactivating selected activities.
CMA CGM reports operations partly resumed under constraints, with high yard occupancy, staff shortages and the Cali to Buenaventura corridor not fully restored.

cause.text: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake damaged infrastructure and closed roads to the port, as reported by carriers and trade press.
cause.attributed_by: Maersk, APM Terminals and CMA CGM, as reported

events.no_effect_note: Buenaventura has no exported PortWatch series in our data.

events.title: Typhoon Dolphin halts container terminals at Ningbo and Shanghai
events.severity_basis: Measured effects at two ports; the portwatch-port-calls series records zero or near zero calls at Ningbo and Shanghai between 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-10, against daily means of about 49 and 88 in the preceding weeks.
events.summary: Typhoon Dolphin shut container handling at Ningbo-Zhoushan and Shanghai in early August 2026. Terminals at Ningbo suspended empty and laden container gate operations from 2026-08-07 (7 August 2026), and the Yangshan and Waigaoqiao terminals at Shanghai followed on 2026-08-08 (8 August 2026), ahead of a landfall in Zhejiang province on 2026-08-09 (9 August 2026). Ningbo terminals restarted on the afternoon of 2026-08-10 and Shanghai early on 2026-08-11. Ships had sheltered outside the anchorages and returned together, so waiting times of several days and carrier port omissions followed for weeks, and one carrier-side estimate put stranded capacity above 2.4 million TEU. Our port call series show Ningbo and Shanghai logging zero or near zero calls on the closure days.

timeline.text: Ningbo-Zhoushan terminals, including Beilun, Daxie and Meishan, suspend empty container gate operations at midday and laden container gate operations in the evening as the typhoon approaches.
Shanghai's Yangshan and Waigaoqiao terminals suspend empty and laden container gate-in and pickup, so both major East China hubs are stopped.
Dolphin comes ashore on the Zhejiang coast; vessels bound for the two ports wait outside the anchorage areas.
Terminal activity at Ningbo restarts on the afternoon of Monday 10 August.
Shanghai resumes operations early on Tuesday 11 August.
Vessel data show 117 ships back in the Shanghai anchorage and 60 in the Ningbo area, with congestion spreading to Southern China.

cause.text: Terminal operators suspended gate and berth operations ahead of the typhoon after China's National Meteorological Center and flood control authorities issued warnings and emergency responses for Zhejiang and Fujian.
cause.attributed_by: Terminal operators and Chinese weather authorities, as reported by logistics firms

resolution.text: Ningbo terminals resumed on the afternoon of 2026-08-10 and Shanghai early on 2026-08-11. A backlog of vessels and cargo persisted for weeks afterwards.

events.title: River pilots stop work on the Parana corridor in Argentina
events.severity_basis: Press reported that Argentina's main ports, including the Greater Rosario hub, stopped for about four days because ships could not move without pilots, which is a simultaneous stoppage of the principal ports of one country.
organisations: Professional Association of Captains and River Guides of the Merchant Marine
events.summary: Starting on 2026-08-01 (1 August 2026), most river and harbour pilots in Argentina stopped accepting new assignments after a presidential decree, published on 31 July, reformed the rules for pilotage. Large vessels cannot move safely on the Parana waterway without a pilot, so ships could not enter or leave ports. Press counts of waiting vessels ranged from about 140 to more than 150, with grain and fuel shipments held up at the Greater Rosario hub. The coast guard ordered pilots back to work and warned of sanctions. On 2026-08-04 the government and the pilots agreed to suspend the decree, cut pilotage tariffs by 20 percent and open a joint working group. Decree 716/2026, published on 2026-08-06, formalised the suspension.

timeline.text: Decree 690/2026 is published. It replaces the 1991 pilotage rules, opens the pilot register without a numerical cap, sets maximum tariffs and lets some foreign captains sail without a local pilot.
Pilots and river guides begin refusing new assignments and honour only services contracted before the stoppage. Ships start to queue unable to enter or leave ports.
Press puts the number of stranded ships at 140 to more than 150. The government and the pilots agree to suspend the decree, cut tariffs by 20 percent and form a working group, and pilots resume work.
Decree 716/2026 is published in the Official Bulletin, suspending the effects of Decree 690/2026 and creating the working group under the Ministry of Security.

cause.text: Pilots stopped taking new work in protest at Decree 690/2026, which the government said was meant to cut logistics costs and open the profession. Their association cited navigation safety and legal uncertainty over liability.

resolution.text: The government and the pilots agreed to suspend the decree, lower pilotage tariffs by 20 percent and set up a joint working group, and pilots returned to work. Decree 716/2026 formalised this on 2026-08-06.

events.title: Record low water at Kaub restricts Rhine barge shipping
events.severity_basis: Barge passage at the Rhine's shallowest point, Kaub, was reported effectively blocked in mid-August 2026, a restriction on the main inland route to Rotterdam; no measured port series covers inland barge traffic, so this is an editor judgment.
events.summary: Low water on the Rhine fell to the lowest level since records began in 1880 at the Kaub gauge, the river's shallowest point, in August 2026, according to trade reporting on 2026-08-11 (11 August 2026). A shipping broker said the river was effectively impassable at Kaub in both directions, barges that did sail carried much lighter loads, and chemical, steel and energy companies moved freight to rail and road. Forecasters said sustained rain would be needed and the problem could last into October. On 2026-08-12 Maersk told customers that barge transport might become operationally infeasible and published low water surcharges. On 2026-10-01 (1 October 2026) the federal hydrology agency reported that the extreme low water was continuing and that rain expected until mid-October would not be enough to end it, so the end date is open.

timeline.text: Levels at Kaub are reported at the lowest since records began in 1880, with a shipping broker saying barges cannot pass in either direction and companies shifting cargo to rail and road, and forecasters saying the problem could last into October.
Maersk warns that barge transport on the Rhine may become operationally unfeasible and publishes low water surcharges and a level below which loading is not guaranteed.

The federal hydrology agency reports that the extreme low water on the federal waterways is continuing, that rain forecast until mid-October will not be enough to end it, and that Kaub is probably staying in the extreme low water range over the next fortnight.

cause.text: Bloomberg reporting links the low river level to dry weather and a heat wave across Europe, with weeks of sustained rain needed for recovery.
cause.attributed_by: Bloomberg, as reported by gCaptain

events.no_effect_note: The disruption is to inland barge traffic on the Rhine, which is not measured by the port call and chokepoint series in our data. Rotterdam sea port calls are not a measure of barge movements.

events.title: Houthi embargo on Saudi shipping and attacks at Bab el-Mandeb
events.severity_basis: A restriction at a chokepoint. Measured on top of the Red Sea diversion (wfm-effect-1.1): PortWatch tanker transits at Bab el-Mandeb 8.5 a day from 2026-07-20 to 2026-09-13 against 13.7 expected, down 38 percent; total transits down 23 percent, below the 25 percent needed for level 4.
events.summary: On 2026-07-20 (20 July 2026) Yemen's Houthis declared a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia, prohibiting vessels loading or discharging at Saudi ports, days after an attack on Sanaa airport. Two days later a US Navy-led maritime information centre warned that the group had positioned missiles and drones near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, and ship trackers saw four tankers with Saudi cargo turn back. On 2026-08-11 the Egyptian-owned Tihamah was hit in the strait, in what Al Jazeera described as the first shipping deaths tied to the Houthis since the Iran war began. IMF PortWatch tanker transits fell from about 14 a day to about 9. The sources are press reports only.

timeline.text: The Houthis declare a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia with immediate effect.
A maritime security centre warns that Houthi missiles and drones are in place near the strait, and tankers with Saudi cargo turn back.
A cargo ship named Tihamah is struck by missiles in Bab el-Mandeb, and a second missile hits the rescue effort, according to Yemen government statements reported by Al Jazeera.

cause.text: The Houthis said the embargo answered what they call a Saudi siege of their ports and airports; the announcement followed an attack on Sanaa airport the week before, and the wider US and Israel war with Iran was ongoing.
cause.attributed_by: Houthi statement as reported by Al Jazeera

events.title: Strait of Hormuz closed to most shipping during the Iran war
events.severity_basis: IMF PortWatch daily transits fell to single digits from 2026-03-02 and stayed there for more than six months, a reduction well above 50% at a chokepoint for over 30 days.
events.summary: Commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz collapsed from 2026-03-01 (1 March 2026), after United States and Israeli strikes on Iran began on 2026-02-28. On 2026-03-02 an adviser to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced the strait closed and threatened any ship that tried to pass. Reporting put pre-war traffic at about 100 vessels a day, and IMF PortWatch counted single digits a day from 2026-03-02. A United States naval blockade of Iranian ports began in April. A memorandum signed on 2026-06-17 reopened the strait for about three weeks at roughly 28 transits a day, before it broke down in July and the blockade resumed on 2026-07-14. By 2026-09-30 the International Maritime Organization had confirmed 88 incidents involving vessels and 24 seafarer deaths. The disruption is ongoing.

timeline.text: United States and Israeli strikes on Iran begin the war. The International Maritime Organization dates the start of the crisis in the strait to this day.

A United States naval blockade of Iranian ports begins. Traffic stays near five vessels a day through the April ceasefire and the blockade.
The International Maritime Organization Secretary-General says there is no safe transit anywhere in the strait, with 29 verified attacks on ships and at least 10 seafarers killed.
The United States and Iran sign a memorandum and the waterway reopens. From 2026-06-18 to 2026-07-05, 513 ships transit, about 28 a day.
After attacks on three vessels on 2026-07-06 and 2026-07-07, the United States president declares the truce over and strikes escalate.
The United States resumes its blockade of Iranian ports. From 2026-07-15, traffic falls back to about five vessels a day.
The International Maritime Organization reports at least 70 verified attacks on shipping, 19 seafarers killed and about 6,000 seafarers stranded in the Gulf.
The blockade continues as the United States and Iran trade strikes on tankers and warships, and Iran warns ships to use only routes it designates.

A seafarer dies when the vessel Cape Dao is damaged about 15 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman. It is one of the fatalities the International Maritime Organization has added to its confirmed count since late August.

The United States president rejects an Iranian plan to reopen the strait within seven days in return for lifting the blockade, easing oil sanctions and releasing frozen funds. The blockade stays in place.

The Kuwaiti crude tanker Al Funtas is struck in the strait while transiting without broadcasting its position. A fire starts and is put out, and the ship carries on. The International Maritime Organization lists it as damaged with no pollution.

UK Maritime Trade Operations reports three tankers struck by unknown projectiles in and around the strait, in delayed reports. The International Maritime Organization confirms damage to two of them, Mersin Prosperity and Sinbad. No party is named as responsible.
The International Maritime Organization counts 88 confirmed incidents involving vessels in the region and 24 confirmed seafarer deaths, up from at least 70 incidents and 19 deaths on 2026-08-28.
A further tanker is struck by an unknown projectile at about 17:50 UTC and catches fire. Its crew is reported safe. The Joint Maritime Information Center keeps the regional threat level at severe.

The Islamic Republic of Iran Customs Administration said clearance for foreign transit, exports and imports restarted at the port on 2025-04-27, and the Ports and Maritime Organization said loading and unloading continued at the remaining terminals and yards, with 26 ships alongside. Fires at the site were reported extinguished on 2025-04-28. Officials said removing damaged containers could take up to two weeks. The Iranian interior ministry attributed the explosion to safety failures, and a government investigation was ordered.

timeline.text: An explosion and fire break out in a container storage area at Shahid Rajaee Port near Bandar Abbas.
The customs administration says clearance for foreign transit, exports and imports has resumed at the port, starting with essential goods and production shipments.
Fires at the port are reported extinguished about two days after the blast. Officials say sporadic fires continued in flammable cargo and that clearing damaged containers could take up to two weeks.
The Ports and Maritime Organization says loading and unloading are running normally at the unaffected terminals and yards, with 26 ships alongside, and that rebuilding of the damaged area has begun.

cause.text: Iranian officials said the explosion involved chemicals stored in containers at the port and pointed to safety failures, and the interior ministry said people at fault had been identified and summoned. A government investigation was ordered and its findings had not been tested in court.
cause.attributed_by: Iranian Ministry of Interior and the government investigation into the explosion

resolution.text: Customs clearance restarted on 2025-04-27 and fires were reported extinguished on 2025-04-28. The port authority said cargo handling at the undamaged terminals and yards was running normally, while clearing the damaged container area continued.

events.title: Lockout of longshore workers closes Port of Montreal terminals
events.severity_basis: Port wide stoppage of 24 hours to seven days; longshore work at the Port of Montreal stopped from 21:00 on 2024-11-10 until terminals restarted at 07:00 on 2024-11-16.
organisations: Canadian Union of Public Employees Local 375
events.summary: On 2024-11-10 (10 November 2024) the Maritime Employers Association locked out about 1,200 longshore workers at the Port of Montreal from 21:00, after members of Canadian Union of Public Employees Local 375 voted 99.7 percent against what the association called its final offer. Container handling stopped, while the port authority said the Bickerdike, liquid bulk and grain terminals would keep working. The lockout followed an overtime strike from 2024-10-10 and an open ended strike at the two Termont terminals from 2024-10-31. On 2024-11-12 the federal labour minister directed the Canada Industrial Relations Board to order operations to resume and to impose binding arbitration. Work restarted at 07:00 on 2024-11-16 (16 November 2024) under a board order.

timeline.text: An open ended strike begins at the two Termont terminals at 11:00, following an overtime strike across the port from 2024-10-10.
The employers' association submits what it calls its final offer and sets a deadline of 20:00 on 2024-11-10 for a reply.
Members vote 99.7 percent to reject the offer and the association locks out longshore workers from 21:00. The port authority says the Bickerdike, liquid bulk and grain terminals stay open.
The federal labour minister directs the Canada Industrial Relations Board to order that operations resume at the ports and to impose final and binding arbitration.
The labour board orders operations at the Port of Montreal to resume at 07:00 on 2024-11-16, with work assignments issued the evening before.
Longshore workers return at 07:00 at all terminals. The port authority says clearing the goods waiting at the port and in transit will take weeks.

cause.text: The employers' association locked out longshore workers after members of Canadian Union of Public Employees Local 375 rejected its final offer, in a dispute over pay and scheduling that had run since the collective agreement expired on 2023-12-31. cause.attributed_by: Maritime Employers Association and Canadian Union of Public Employees Local 375

resolution.text: After the federal labour minister directed binding arbitration, the Canada Industrial Relations Board ordered operations to resume and longshore work restarted at 07:00 on 2024-11-16 at all Port of Montreal terminals, with the previous agreement extended.

events.title: Lockout of ship and dock foremen stops British Columbia ports

organisations: International Longshore and Warehouse Union Ship and Dock Foremen Local 514
events.summary: On 2024-11-04 (4 November 2024) the British Columbia Maritime Employers Association locked out more than 700 ship and dock foremen of International Longshore and Warehouse Union Local 514 at terminals across British Columbia, hours after the union began industry wide strike activity at 08:00. The lockout began on the 16:30 shift and did not apply to grain or cruise operations. Container work at Vancouver and Prince Rupert stopped. Talks broke off on 2024-11-09. On 2024-11-12 (12 November 2024) the federal labour minister directed the Canada Industrial Relations Board to order operations to resume and to impose binding arbitration. The board issued its order on 2024-11-13 and terminals restarted on 2024-11-14, with dispatching on the day shift and operations from 16:30.

timeline.text: Local 514 begins industry wide strike activity at about 08:00, and the employers' association locks out foremen and other Local 514 members from the 16:30 shift, excluding grain and cruise work.

The labour board orders the employers' association and its members to resume operations on 2024-11-14 and to continue them until it makes a final determination.

Operations restart, with dispatching on the day shift and maintenance and terminal operations from the 16:30 shift. The board schedules a hearing for 2024-11-18 on questions raised about the ministerial direction.

cause.text: The employers' association said it locked out Local 514 members in response to the union's strike notice and strike activity, to allow a safe and orderly wind down of operations after nearly two years of bargaining for a new agreement. events.title: Dockworkers strike halts US East and Gulf Coast container ports
events.severity_basis: Port wide stoppage of 24 hours to seven days; container terminals from Maine to Texas stopped work from 2024-10-01 until job actions ceased on the evening of 2024-10-03.
events.summary: From 2024-10-01 (1 October 2024) members of the International Longshoremen's Association struck container terminals at ports from Maine to Texas after contract talks with the United States Maritime Alliance failed, the union's first coastwide stoppage on the Atlantic and Gulf coasts in decades. The union said work stopped at 00:01 on 2024-10-01 at all Atlantic and Gulf Coast ports. Terminals at New York and New Jersey, Baltimore, Norfolk, Wilmington, Charleston, Savannah, Brunswick and Houston closed to vessel and gate operations, while automated and non ILA facilities continued. On the evening of 2024-10-03 (3 October 2024) the two sides announced a tentative wage agreement and an extension of the master contract to 2025-01-15, and said all job actions would cease immediately. Ports reopened through 2024-10-04.

timeline.text: The strike begins at 00:01 local time after the master contract expires, stopping container work at ports from Maine to Texas, among them the terminals at Newark and Boston reported by the trade press.
Four northeastern governors call on both sides to settle and say they will watch for price gouging while the stoppage continues.
The union and the employers' alliance announce a tentative agreement on wages and an extension of the master contract to 2025-01-15, stating that "all current job actions will cease" immediately.
Terminals reopen through the day. The Georgia Ports Authority resumes truck gates at Garden City Terminal at 06:00 and rail at 07:00, with vessel work at Brunswick that evening.

cause.text: The union struck after negotiations with the United States Maritime Alliance over a new master contract broke down on wages and on protections against automation. The dispute ended with a tentative wage settlement and a contract extension, with automation left to further bargaining.
cause.attributed_by: International Longshoremen's Association and United States Maritime Alliance

resolution.text: The union and the employers' alliance reached a tentative agreement on wages on the evening of 2024-10-03, extended the master contract to 2025-01-15 and said all job actions would cease immediately. Terminals resumed work through 2024-10-04.

events.title: Hurricane Helene closes the Port Tampa Bay and Port Manatee shipping channels
events.severity_basis: Port wide stoppage of 24 hours to seven days; Port Tampa Bay stopped inbound and outbound vessel traffic from 20:00 on 2024-09-25 and its channels reopened at 13:15 on 2024-09-29, about 3.7 days.
events.summary: At 20:00 local time on 2024-09-25 (25 September 2024) the Coast Guard set Port Condition Zulu for Tampa Bay ahead of Hurricane Helene, and Port Tampa Bay halted inbound and outbound vessel traffic. A shipping agent's bulletin dated 2024-09-27 still listed Tampa and Port Manatee as closed while the Coast Guard's reopening advice was awaited. Channel surveys with the Army Corps of Engineers began that day. On 2024-09-29 (29 September 2024) the Coast Guard reopened the port under restrictions and the port said ship movements were limited to daylight hours. Fuel tankers, cruise ships and vessels carrying perishable cargo were to return first, and fuel deliveries by land continued throughout.

timeline.text: At 20:00 the Coast Guard sets Port Condition Zulu, meaning gale force winds may reach the port within 12 hours. Inbound and outbound vessel traffic stops and the shipping channels close, while landside operations continue.

Port Tampa Bay works with the Coast Guard and the Army Corps of Engineers to begin surveying its channels. A shipping agent's bulletin lists Tampa and Port Manatee as closed with the storm past and the Coast Guard's advice on reopening awaited.

The Coast Guard reopens the port and sets the condition to normal with restrictions. Port Tampa Bay says channels are open to ship movements in daylight hours only and that fuel tankers, cruise ships and perishable cargo vessels will arrive first.

cause.text: The Coast Guard set Port Condition Zulu ahead of Hurricane Helene, a step the port described as a response to the chance of gale force winds within 12 hours. The Coast Guard reopened the port after assessments of the port, waterways and channels.
cause.attributed_by: U.S. Coast Guard

resolution.text: After assessments of the port, waterways and channels, the Coast Guard reopened the port on 2024-09-29 under restrictions, with ship movements limited to daylight hours. Port Tampa Bay said it hoped the channels would be at full depth shortly.

events.title: Typhoon Yagi halts container handling at Hong Kong and Shenzhen terminals
events.severity_basis: Hong Kong terminals stopped deliveries at 12:00 on 2024-09-05 and the No. 8 signal stayed up until 12:40 on 2024-09-06, with Yantian pick-up suspensions from 03:00 on 2024-09-05, which falls in the band of 24 hours to 7 days at port level.
organisations: Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
events.summary: Super Typhoon Yagi stopped container handling at terminals in Hong Kong and Shenzhen between 2024-09-04 (4 September 2024) and 2024-09-06 (6 September 2024). Shekou and Hong Kong stopped releasing empty containers at 23:00 on 2024-09-04, and Yantian did the same at 03:00 on 2024-09-05. Hong Kong's main container terminals stopped all deliveries at noon that day. The Hong Kong Observatory raised the No. 8 signal at 18:20 on 2024-09-05 and replaced it with the No. 3 signal at 12:40 on 2024-09-06 as the storm moved away. Yantian stopped laden pick-up and delivery at 23:00 on 2024-09-05. The sources reviewed give no time at which the terminals reopened.

timeline.text: Shekou Container Terminal suspends empty and laden pick-up and laden delivery at 23:00, and Hong Kong suspends empty container pick-up at 23:00.

Yantian stops empty container handling at 03:00. Hong Kong Container Terminals 4, 6 and 7, COSCO-HIT and Asia Container Terminals stop all deliveries at 12:00. The Observatory issues the No. 8 signal at 18:20, and Yantian suspends laden pick-up and delivery at 23:00.
The Observatory replaces the No. 8 signal with the No. 3 signal at 12:40 as Yagi moves away from Hong Kong.

cause.text: Terminal handling stopped as Typhoon Yagi, classed by the Hong Kong Observatory as a super typhoon, passed to the south-west of Hong Kong with gales expected near the Pearl River Estuary.
cause.attributed_by: Hong Kong Observatory, as reported by Container News

resolution.text: The Hong Kong Observatory lowered the storm signal from No. 8 to No. 3 at 12:40 on 2024-09-06; the sources reviewed do not say when each terminal resumed handling.

events.title: CN and CPKC lock out rail workers and stop Canadian freight rail
events.severity_basis: Rail service that carries about two thirds of Port of Vancouver cargo stopped for under 24 hours on CN and from 2024-08-22 until a restart at 00:01 Eastern on 2024-08-26 on CPKC; no measured port effect has been computed yet, so level 2 is provisional.
events.summary: On 2024-08-22 (22 August 2024) Canadian National Railway (CN) and Canadian Pacific Kansas City (CPKC) locked out members of the Teamsters Canada Rail Conference, and freight trains stopped on both railways at once. The federal labour minister used section 107 of the Canada Labour Code the same day to send the dispute to the Canada Industrial Relations Board for binding arbitration. CN ended its lockout at 18:00 Eastern that evening. The board's order of 2024-08-24 led CPKC to restart operations from 00:01 Eastern on 2024-08-26 (26 August 2024). The Vancouver Fraser Port Authority said that rail carries about two thirds of its cargo and that a full recovery would take time, while the mayor of Prince Rupert warned of damage to a town built around its port.

timeline.text: CN notifies the union that it will lock out its members at 00:01 Eastern on 2024-08-22 unless an agreement or binding arbitration comes first, and says it is shutting its network down in phases, with more embargoes due on 2024-08-19.

The Port of Vancouver warns shippers to expect rail disruption from 2024-08-22, after both railways issued lockout notices and the union issued a strike notice to CPKC. The port authority changes how it assigns anchorages and asks ship operators to slow down so they arrive close to their berth time.

Both railways lock out their union-represented staff and the first simultaneous stoppage at the two railways begins. The labour minister directs the labour board to impose binding arbitration and resume operations, and CN ends its lockout at 18:00 Eastern. The Vancouver Fraser Port Authority says most terminals will feel the effect.

The labour board orders binding arbitration, bars any further strike or lockout during the process and extends the current agreements. The union says it will comply and appeal in federal court, and CPKC announces that it will restart on 2024-08-26.

Most union members at both railways return to work. The Vancouver Fraser Port Authority says rail service is resuming at the port and that its focus is a recovery plan, including prioritised anchorage use.

cause.text: CN and CPKC locked out Teamsters Canada Rail Conference members when no new agreement or binding arbitration was in place at the deadlines in their notices. CN said the union had refused its offers; the union said it was protecting rail safety and working conditions, including against forced relocation of workers.
cause.attributed_by: CN, CPKC and Teamsters Canada Rail Conference

resolution.text: After the labour board ordered binding arbitration and extended the existing agreements, CN resumed train movements from the evening of 2024-08-22 and CPKC restarted from 00:01 Eastern on 2024-08-26, when most union members returned to work.

events.title: Hurricane Beryl closes the Houston, Galveston, Freeport and Texas City ports
events.severity_basis: Port wide stoppage of 24 hours to seven days at Houston; the Coast Guard closed the port on 2024-07-07, Port Houston terminals stayed shut through 2024-07-09 and the Houston Ship Channel had no draft restrictions from 2024-07-11.
events.summary: On 2024-07-07 (7 July 2024) the Coast Guard closed the ports of Houston, Galveston, Freeport and Texas City ahead of Hurricane Beryl, which came ashore near Matagorda, Texas, as a category 1 storm on 2024-07-08. Port Houston announced that its terminals would stay closed through 2024-07-09 and said operations would restart on 2024-07-10. The Captain of the Port moved all four ports to the recovery condition on 2024-07-09. On 2024-07-11 the Greater Houston Port Bureau said the Houston Ship Channel no longer had draft restrictions, while Galveston, Texas City and Freeport still had limits and Freeport allowed daylight movements only.

timeline.text: The Coast Guard declares Port Condition Zulu at Houston, Galveston, Freeport and Texas City, which stops vessel transits and cargo operations in those ports.

Beryl makes landfall near Matagorda, Texas. Port Houston says its terminals will stay closed through 2024-07-09, and the Coast Guard sets up a Unified Command to restore the marine transportation system.
The Captain of the Port Houston-Galveston sets Port Condition Recovery for the ports of Houston, Texas City, Galveston and Freeport after waterway assessments.
Port Houston resumes operations, after offering extended gate hours at its container terminals the previous day.
The Greater Houston Port Bureau reports all Houston Ship Channel restrictions lifted. Draft limits remain at Galveston (35 feet), Texas City (30 feet) and Freeport (36 feet, daylight only).

events.title: Container ships wait for berths at the Port of Singapore
events.severity_basis: Berth waiting of two to three days, and longer in some cases, affected one port for several weeks without a stoppage, which sits at the moderate level for a port level disruption of more than 24 hours.
organisations: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore
events.summary: Container ships waited longer for berths at the Port of Singapore from May 2024, and the port operator said waiting had fallen back to two days or less by 2024-07-10 (10 July 2024). The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore said on 2024-05-30 (30 May 2024) that the average wait for a container berth was about two to three days, that about 90 percent of container ships were arriving off schedule against about 77 percent in 2023, and that diversions around the Cape of Good Hope had bunched arrivals. Container volumes in the first four months of 2024 were 13.36 million TEU, 8.8 percent above the same months of 2023. PSA reactivated berths and yard space at Keppel Terminal, opened further berths at Tuas Port and added staff.

timeline.text: The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore says the average wait for a container berth is about two to three days, blames off schedule arrivals and higher volumes, and reports weekly handling raised by PSA from 770,000 to 820,000 TEU.

A further berth opens at Tuas Port, with more planned for October and December, as trade press reports about 90 percent of container ships arriving off schedule and waits of up to seven days in some cases.
PSA says the average wait has come down to two days or less in recent weeks, and that it moved 7 percent more container volume in the first half of 2024 than a year earlier.

cause.text: The authority said ships diverting around the Cape of Good Hope had disrupted arrival schedules worldwide and caused bunching, and that off schedule arrivals together with higher container volumes handled in Singapore had lengthened waits for a container berth.
cause.attributed_by: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore

resolution.text: Waiting for a berth fell back to two days or less by 2024-07-10 after PSA reactivated berths and yard space at Keppel Terminal, commissioned further berths at Tuas Port and added frontline staff.

events.title: Ship strikes Key Bridge and closes the Baltimore ship channel
events.severity_basis: Port closure of seven days or more; the deep draft channel serving the Port of Baltimore was blocked from 2024-03-26 until its restoration on 2024-06-10.
organisations: U.S. Navy Supervisor of Salvage and Diving
events.summary: On 2024-03-26 (26 March 2024) the container ship Dali lost electrical power on departure from Baltimore and struck a pier of the Francis Scott Key Bridge, which collapsed into the Patapsco River and blocked the Fort McHenry Federal Channel, the deep draft approach to the Port of Baltimore. Six highway workers on the bridge were killed. Temporary alternate channels for shallow draft vessels opened in early April, and a limited access channel 300 feet wide and 35 feet deep followed on 2024-04-25. The Dali was refloated on 2024-05-20 and the channel was widened to 400 feet. The Army Corps of Engineers and the Navy Supervisor of Salvage and Diving announced on 2024-06-10 (10 June 2024) that the channel had been restored to 700 feet wide and 50 feet deep after about 50,000 tons of wreckage were removed.

timeline.text: The Dali contacts a pier of the Francis Scott Key Bridge at about 01:29 local time after a loss of electrical power. The bridge falls across the main ship channel, ending deep draft access to the Port of Baltimore.
The first temporary alternate channel opens around the wreckage for shallow draft vessels, the first of the interim routes used while the main channel stays blocked.
A limited access channel 300 feet wide and 35 feet deep opens through the wreckage.
The Dali is refloated and moved from the site, and the federal channel is opened at 400 feet wide and 50 feet deep.
The Unified Command surveys the riverbed and certifies it safe for transit, and the Army Corps of Engineers and the Navy announce the channel restored to 700 feet wide and 50 feet deep.
The National Transportation Safety Board adopts its final report, finding the probable cause to be a blackout caused by a loose signal wire connection at a terminal block.

cause.text: The National Transportation Safety Board determined that the probable cause was a loss of electrical power caused by a loose signal wire connection to a terminal block, which stemmed from the improper installation of wire label banding and left the vessel without propulsion or steering near the bridge. The board said the bridge lacked countermeasures against a strike by an ocean going ship.
cause.attributed_by: National Transportation Safety Board

resolution.text: Wreckage removal by the Army Corps of Engineers and the Navy Supervisor of Salvage and Diving restored the Fort McHenry Federal Channel to 700 feet wide and 50 feet deep on 2024-06-10, returning the Port of Baltimore to unrestricted deep draft access.

events.title: Gang violence halts container and oil terminals at Port-au-Prince
events.severity_basis: The main container terminal at Port-au-Prince received no container ships for about a month from the week of 2024-03-04, and the Varreux oil terminal was closed from 2024-04-22 until 2024-05-03, a port-level closure of more than 7 days.
events.summary: From the week of 2024-03-04 (4 March 2024), gang violence in Port-au-Prince left the capital's main seaport largely idle. A Logistics Sector update dated 2024-03-15 reported that the national port facility was not fully operational, that Caribbean Port Services (CPS), the main container terminal operator, was not working, and that more than 300 aid containers were stranded. A Haitian newspaper reported on 2024-04-04 that no container ship had docked at CPS for a month and that no arrival date was set. The UN humanitarian office (OCHA) reported that the Varreux oil terminal was closed from 2024-04-22 after repeated attacks and reopened on 2024-05-03. On 2024-05-23 OCHA still described seaport operations as irregular. The sources found do not say when container shipping resumed at CPS.

timeline.text: Port activity is halted or sharply reduced after violence engulfs the capital from 2024-02-29. No container ship docks at CPS from about this week, according to a later press report.

The Logistics Sector reports that the national port facility is not fully operational and that CPS is not working but may resume soon. More than 300 aid containers are stranded and at risk of looting.
A Haitian newspaper reports that no container ship has docked at CPS for a month, and that an official source has no date for the next arrivals.
The Varreux oil terminal is closed after repeated attacks by armed groups, raising fears of fuel supply problems.
OCHA reports that the Logistics Sector has retrieved more than 100 humanitarian containers from CPS over the previous three weeks.
The Varreux oil terminal reopens, and diesel and gasoline are shipped out between 2024-05-03 and 2024-05-06.
OCHA reports that several dozen humanitarian containers remain blocked at the port and describes seaport operations as irregular.

cause.text: OCHA and the Logistics Sector attributed the closures to violence and repeated attacks by armed groups in and around Port-au-Prince. No source cited here attributes the attacks to a named group.
cause.attributed_by: UN OCHA and the Logistics Sector

resolution.text: The Varreux oil terminal reopened on 2024-05-03. events.title: Attacks on shipping in the Red Sea divert traffic around Africa
events.severity_basis: A disruption documented by official sources across more than one region at once; governments and carriers have recorded attacks in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden and the rerouting of services around the Cape of Good Hope since 2023.
events.summary: On 2023-11-19 (19 November 2023) the vehicle carrier Galaxy Leader was seized in the Red Sea near Hodeidah, the first in a run of attacks on merchant ships that the United Kingdom government and other states attribute to the Houthi movement. Attacks with missiles, drones and boarding parties followed through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Gulf of Aden. From 2023-12-15 (15 December 2023) Maersk paused its ships bound for the strait and then routed services around the Cape of Good Hope, and other carriers did the same, moving a large share of Asia to Europe traffic off the Suez route. Attacks paused between late 2025 and early 2026 and some services returned, then threats and rerouting resumed. As of 2026-09-15 (15 September 2026) no dated official announcement records an end.

The United Kingdom government condemns what it calls the unlawful seizure of the ship by the Houthis and demands the release of vessel and crew.
Maersk instructs all of its vessels bound for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to pause, citing a near miss involving one of its ships the day before and a further attack on a container ship.
Maersk says the paused ships will instead sail around Africa by way of the Cape of Good Hope.
After an attack on one of its ships, Maersk pauses all transits through the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden until further notice and diverts them around the Cape.

After a pause in attacks from about November 2025, officials of the group are reported as saying they will resume attacks on merchant ships, and Maersk again moves selected services to the Cape route.
Reporting from the region describes Houthi control of the Yemeni Red Sea coast and says operators are still routing around the Cape rather than through the strait.

cause.text: The United Kingdom government attributes the seizure of the Galaxy Leader and the wider campaign against merchant shipping to the Houthi movement, and says Iran has provided it with military and political support. events.summary: On 2023-11-10 (10 November 2023) DP World Australia detected unauthorised access to its Australian corporate network and disconnected that network from the internet, which stopped landside operations at its container terminals in Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane and Fremantle. Operations restarted on 2023-11-13 (13 November 2023), and the company said the resumption did not mean the incident had concluded. events.title: Vessel congestion at the Port of Durban container terminals
events.severity_basis: Port level disruption well beyond seven days; Transnet said in November 2023 that clearing the container backlog would take up to seven weeks at Pier 1 and 15 weeks at Pier 2.

Reporting at the time counted more than 60 vessels off the port. Transnet said clearing the backlog would take up to seven weeks at Pier 1 and 15 weeks at Pier 2. By early January 2024 the queue had fallen to about five vessels at anchor, which Transnet attributed to holiday period staffing and faster access to spare parts.

events.title: Russia ends Black Sea Grain Initiative participation and strikes Ukrainian ports

A senior United Nations official told the Security Council that port infrastructure at Odesa and Mykolaiv was being targeted and that more than 60,000 tonnes of grain had been destroyed. events.title: Ransomware stops container handling at the Port of Nagoya
events.severity_basis: Port wide stoppage of 24 hours to 7 days; container work stopped at every Nagoya terminal from 2023-07-04 until 2023-07-06.
events.summary: On 2023-07-04 (4 July 2023) the Nagoya Port Unified Terminal System stopped working at about 06:30 local time, and container work stopped at every terminal in the port. The Nagoya Harbor Transportation Association reported that a ransom note printed from a system printer at about 07:30, that the servers were found encrypted that afternoon, and that the Aichi Prefectural Police and the system maintenance company assessed the cause as a ransomware infection. Restoration from backups finished on 2023-07-06 (6 July 2023) and terminals restarted in sequence from 15:00, with the last resuming at 18:15. The association said no ransom amount was stated and that it did not contact the attackers. Press reports attributed the attack to the LockBit group.

resolution.text: Systems were restored from backups and terminal work resumed in sequence on 2023-07-06, with the final terminals restarting at 18:15. The association said it found no evidence of data leaving the organisation.

events.title: Longshore strike stops cargo at British Columbia ports
events.severity_basis: Port closure of seven days or more; cargo work stopped across British Columbia terminals for 13 days from 2023-07-01 to 2023-07-13, with a further stoppage on 2023-07-18.
organisations: International Longshore and Warehouse Union Canada
events.summary: From 2023-07-01 (1 July 2023) longshore workers represented by the International Longshore and Warehouse Union Canada struck terminals across British Columbia, including Vancouver and Prince Rupert, in a dispute with the British Columbia Maritime Employers Association over wages, contracting out and automation. The union caucus then rejected the terms and members returned to picket lines at 16:30 on 2023-07-18. The Canada Industrial Relations Board ruled that action unlawful for want of 72 hours notice, and the union withdrew a fresh strike notice on 2023-07-19 (19 July 2023). A negotiated agreement followed on 2023-07-30 and was ratified in early August.

events.title: Cyclone Biparjoy suspends operations at Gujarat ports

events.title: Drought cuts draft and daily transits at the Panama Canal
events.severity_basis: A restriction at a chokepoint that ran for more than a year, with the number of daily booking slots cut from about 32 to 22 and the Neopanamax draft cut from 15.24 m to 13.41 m; no measured effect is available yet, so this rests on the non measured chokepoint criteria.
events.summary: From 2023-03-01 (1 March 2023) the Panama Canal Authority cut the maximum authorised draft in the Neopanamax locks below its normal 15.24 m (50 feet), the first of a series of reductions caused by low water in Gatun Lake. The draft fell in steps to 13.41 m (44 feet) during June 2023, and from 2023-07-30 (30 July 2023) the authority also limited daily transit capacity to an average of 32 vessels. After the driest October in its records, the authority cut booking slots to 25, then 24, then 22 a day in December 2023, and scheduled further cuts to 20 and 18 that it later cancelled. Rain from late 2023 allowed 24 slots a day from 2024-01-16. The draft returned to 15.24 m on 2024-08-15 and 36 daily booking slots resumed for transit dates from 2024-09-01.

timeline.text: The canal authority announces that from 2023-03-01 the maximum authorised draft in the Neopanamax locks will be 15.09 m (49.5 feet), below the normal 15.24 m (50 feet), and says further cuts will come in steps of about 15 cm.
The authority announces drafts of 13.56 m (44.5 feet) from 2023-05-24 and 13.41 m (44.0 feet) from 2023-05-30 in the Neopanamax locks.
Rain allows the authority to postpone the 13.41 m (44.0 feet) draft to 2023-06-13, keeping 13.56 m (44.5 feet) until 2023-06-12, with 13.26 m (43.5 feet) then scheduled for 2023-06-25.

The authority sets daily transit capacity at an average of 32 vessels from 2023-07-30, split 10 in the Neopanamax locks and 22 in the Panamax locks, and says it expects to hold the draft at 13.41 m (44 feet) for the following months.

After the lowest October rainfall in its records since 1950, the authority cuts booking slots to 25 for 2023-11-03 to 2023-11-06, 24 to 2023-11-30, 22 in December 2023, 20 in January 2024 and 18 from February 2024.
Better rainfall in late 2023 lets the authority run 24 transits a day instead of the planned reductions, and it says that level will hold until conditions change.
The authority restores the maximum authorised draft in the Neopanamax locks to 15.24 m (50.0 feet) with immediate effect and announces 36 daily booking slots for transit dates from 2024-09-01.

cause.text: The Panama Canal Authority attributed the restrictions to an extended dry season, high evaporation and rainfall well below average in the canal watershed, which lowered Gatun Lake, the fresh water source for the locks. It cited the lowest recorded October rainfall since 1950 and forecast El Nino conditions.
cause.attributed_by: Panama Canal Authority

resolution.text: Water levels recovered enough for the authority to return the Neopanamax draft to 15.24 m (50 feet) on 2024-08-15 and to offer 36 daily booking slots for transit dates from 2024-09-01, which it described as a return to normal operating conditions.

events.title: Earthquake and container fire close Iskenderun port in Turkey
events.severity_basis: The port closed on 2023-02-06 and carriers were still reporting it closed on 2023-03-31, with partial reopening and first trial calls only in the week of 2023-04-10, a closure of more than seven days.
events.summary: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake on 2023-02-06 (6 February 2023) damaged the port of Iskenderun in southern Turkey and set stacked containers on fire. Maersk said the port suffered severe structural damage and all operations stopped, and Turkey's maritime authority told ships to use other ports. events.title: Cargo truckers strike cuts container movement at South Korean ports
events.severity_basis: Landside container movement at the country's 12 main ports, including Busan, Gwangyang, Incheon and Ulsan, was cut for more than seven days, the closest non measured criterion to a port level restriction of seven days or more.

Members voted on 2022-12-09 (9 December 2022) to end the action, with nearly 62 percent of those voting in favour, and trucks returned the same day. Fourteen vessels, 12 outbound and two inbound, use the corridor, and inspectors complete 46 inspections of outbound ships.

events.title: Low water closes two stretches of the Lower Mississippi River to barge traffic
events.severity_basis: Closest rubric match is a stoppage of 24 hours to seven days; the Coast Guard reported a restriction near Stack Island and a closure at Memphis on 2022-10-04 and confirmed both stretches open, with one-way traffic and draft limits, on 2022-10-10.
events.summary: Falling water in the Lower Mississippi River led to barge groundings and, on 2022-10-04 (4 October 2022), a Coast Guard waterway restriction near Stack Island, Mississippi, and a closure at Memphis, Tennessee. The Coast Guard set up a recovery unit with agency and industry partners the next day. Queues grew to more than 100 tow boats at the two sites. Dredging deepened the channel, and on 2022-10-10 the Coast Guard said both stretches had reopened over the preceding weekend, with one-way traffic and limits on barge draft and tow size still in force. NOAA counted 144 vessels and 2,253 barges backed up during October, and the river at Memphis fell to a record low on 2022-10-17.

timeline.text: Barges ground near Stack Island, Mississippi, where a waterway restriction covers river miles 478 to 492, and at Memphis, Tennessee, where the river is closed from mile 686 to mile 676.

More than 100 towboats and tows wait at the two closures while dredging proceeds at Stack Island. A low water advisory covers river miles 303 to 869, and barge operator Ingram declares force majeure for operations downriver of Baton Rouge.
The Coast Guard says both stretches reopened over the weekend after dredging. A southbound queue of 22 tow boats and 392 barges still waits near Stack Island, and traffic stays one-way.
The river gauge at Memphis falls to -10.79 feet, the lowest level recorded there since National Weather Service records began in 1954.

cause.text: The Coast Guard attributed the groundings and closures to low water levels on the Lower Mississippi River. NOAA linked the low water to drought conditions across the basin.
cause.attributed_by: U.S. Coast Guard

resolution.text: Dredging deepened the channel at Stack Island and Memphis and the Coast Guard confirmed both stretches reopened. Restrictions on barge draft and tow size stayed in place and the river kept falling for another week.

events.title: Low water at Kaub restricts Rhine barge shipping in summer 2022
events.severity_basis: The Kaub gauge fell to 31 cm on 2022-08-15 amid extreme low water on the navigable Rhine from mid-July to mid-September 2022, a restriction on the main inland route that no measured series covers, so this is an editor judgment.

events.summary: Low water on the Rhine restricted barge shipping from mid-July to mid-September 2022 (July to September 2022), according to the International Commission for the Protection of the Rhine. At Kaub, the Middle Rhine gauge that shipping watches most closely, the German federal hydrology institute (BfG) recorded 31 cm on 2022-08-15 (15 August 2022), just above the record of 25 cm set on 2018-10-22. The European Space Agency reported that freight vessels were sailing at roughly a quarter to a third of capacity. Rain in late August lifted the gauge to a crest of 128 cm on 2022-08-23, but the BfG said the low water situation had not been resolved. The Central Commission for Navigation on the Rhine counted 41 days at Kaub below the equivalent water level in 2022.

timeline.text: Extremely low water levels set in along the navigable Rhine from mid-July, according to the Rhine protection commission, which had already recorded low flows from March after a dry winter.

The Kaub gauge reads 31 cm, close to the record low of 25 cm from October 2018. Shipping continues with reduced loads. The European Space Agency reports 32 cm at Kaub that day and vessels at about a quarter to a third of capacity.

Rain in Switzerland and the Black Forest lifts Kaub to a crest of 128 cm, barely above the low water range. By 2022-08-25 the level is back to 111 cm and the BfG says the low water situation is not resolved.

Water levels recover gradually from the second half of August. At least average levels hold from October, and the Rhine commission treats the low water event as over. The navigation commission later counts 41 days at Kaub below the equivalent water level of 78 cm for 2022.

cause.text: The Rhine protection commission attributes the low water mainly to below-average rain in spring and summer 2022 combined with above-average air temperatures, after a dry and mild winter 2021/2022 in which no large snow reserves formed.
cause.attributed_by: International Commission for the Protection of the Rhine

resolution.text: The Rhine protection commission reports extremely low water on the navigable Rhine until mid-September 2022, a gradual recovery from the second half of August and at least average levels from October, when it considers the event ended.

events.severity_basis: Simultaneous stoppage of the principal ports of one country, with Hamburg, Bremerhaven, Wilhelmshaven, Bremen, Emden and Brake stopped together for 48 hours from 2022-07-14.
events.summary: Between 2022-06-09 (9 June 2022) and 2022-07-16 (16 July 2022) the union ver.di called three warning strikes at German North Sea ports during a pay round covering about 12,000 port workers. The first stoppage, on 2022-06-09, lasted one shift at Hamburg, Bremerhaven, Wilhelmshaven and Emden, and a second followed later in June. After a sixth round of talks with the Zentralverband der deutschen Seehafenbetriebe ended without agreement, ver.di called a 48 hour stoppage from 06:00 on 2022-07-14 to 06:00 on 2022-07-16 at Hamburg, Bremerhaven, Bremen, Wilhelmshaven, Emden and Brake, the longest such action at these ports in decades. A settlement before the Hamburg labour court paused further action, and the two sides agreed terms on 2022-08-23.

timeline.text: ver.di holds a first warning strike of one shift at Hamburg, Bremerhaven, Wilhelmshaven and Emden after pay talks break down. The union represents about 12,000 port workers.
A sixth round of talks with the employers' association ends without agreement and ver.di calls a 48 hour stoppage, following two shorter warning strikes in June.
Work stops for 48 hours from 06:00 at Hamburg, Bremerhaven, Bremen, Wilhelmshaven, Emden and Brake, in what trade press described as the longest such action at these ports in more than 40 years.
The stoppage ends at 06:00. Further action is paused while talks resume under an arrangement reached at the Hamburg labour court.

ver.di and the employers' association agree terms for about 12,000 workers, with increases from 1 July 2022 of 9.4 per cent in full container operations and 7.9 per cent in conventional and general cargo operations, and an inflation clause.

cause.text: ver.di called the stoppages in the 2022 pay round for German seaports, saying it sought compensation for inflation for about 12,000 workers after successive rounds of talks with the Zentralverband der deutschen Seehafenbetriebe failed to produce an acceptable offer.
cause.attributed_by: ver.di

resolution.text: The strikes ended on 2022-07-16 and further action was paused while negotiations continued. On 2022-08-23 ver.di and the employers' association agreed a settlement with staged increases and an inflation clause, which the union's collective bargaining commission approved on 2022-09-05.

events.title: Shanghai COVID-19 lockdown restricts trucking to the port
events.severity_basis: Landside access to the principal container port of China was restricted for more than two months, the closest non measured criterion to a port level restriction of seven days or more, since the terminals themselves stayed open.
events.summary: Shanghai began a staged COVID-19 lockdown on 2022-03-28 (28 March 2022), starting in Pudong and extending to the rest of the city from 2022-04-01, and lifted citywide restrictions on 2022-06-01 (1 June 2022). The container terminals at Yangshan and Waigaoqiao kept working under closed loop arrangements, and the carrier Maersk reported in early April that terminal operations continued without delay. The restriction fell on the landside: trucking capacity into and out of the city was cut by driver shortages, testing and quarantine rules, and warehouses inside locked down areas stopped work. Carriers shifted boxes to barge and rail and omitted some calls. The city said normal production and daily life would resume from 2022-06-01, and trade press reported container work close to normal levels in early June.

timeline.text: A staged lockdown begins in Pudong, the district that holds part of the port's landside operations, and extends to the rest of the city from 2022-04-01.

Maersk reports that the Yangshan and Waigaoqiao terminals are operating normally for vessel, yard and gate work, while trucking capacity is reduced and warehouses inside locked down areas are affected. No Shanghai calls had been cancelled at that point.
The city government says normal production and daily operations will resume from 2022-06-01, with public transport restarting and most residents free to leave their compounds.
Citywide restrictions are lifted.

Trade press reports Shanghai handled just over 3.4 million TEU in May against a normal month of close to 4 million, with container ship calls down 16 percent against May 2021, and waiting times back near seasonal norms as trucking recovered.

cause.text: The restrictions were COVID-19 control measures ordered by the Shanghai city government during an Omicron outbreak, lifted when the city said the outbreak had been brought under control.
cause.attributed_by: Shanghai Municipal People's Government

resolution.text: The city lifted citywide restrictions from 2022-06-01 and removed limits on which businesses could reopen. Container work at the port returned close to normal levels over the following days, with trucking the slowest part to recover.

events.title: Ukraine's Black Sea ports close to commercial shipping after the invasion
events.severity_basis: Simultaneous stoppage of the principal ports of one country; every Ukrainian Black Sea and Azov Sea port was closed to commercial traffic from 2022-02-24.
events.summary: From 2022-02-24 (24 February 2022) commercial shipping stopped at Ukraine's Black Sea and Azov Sea ports after Russia's invasion, and merchant ships and their crews were left in port. The International Maritime Organization Council met in extraordinary session on 2022-03-10 and 2022-03-11 and agreed to encourage a blue safe maritime corridor so that ships and seafarers could leave the area. Grain exports restarted under the Black Sea Grain Initiative, signed in Istanbul on 2022-07-22, with the first outbound vessel leaving Odesa on 2022-08-01 (1 August 2022). The United Nations said it was the first cargo ship to leave a Ukrainian Black Sea port since 2022-02-26. Movements at Chornomorsk and Pivdennyi followed in August 2022. Mariupol, under Russian control, did not reopen to commercial traffic.

timeline.text: Commercial shipping halts at Ukrainian ports as Russia invades. The Azov Sea closes to commercial traffic, and carriers stop calling at Ukrainian ports.

The International Maritime Organization Council, in extraordinary session, says ships should be allowed to sail from Ukrainian ports without threat of attack and backs a blue safe maritime corridor for seafarers.

The first vessel under the Black Sea Grain Initiative leaves Odesa with 26,527 tonnes of corn for Lebanon. The United Nations says it is the first cargo ship out of a Ukrainian Black Sea port since 2022-02-26.
The Joint Coordination Centre reports authorised movements for vessels bound for Chornomorsk and Pivdennyi, extending the corridor beyond Odesa.

cause.text: Ukrainian authorities suspended commercial shipping at the country's ports after Russia's invasion on 2022-02-24, and Russia closed the Azov Sea to commercial vessels, as reported by Lloyd's List and Ship Technology.
cause.attributed_by: Ukrainian authorities as reported by Lloyd's List and Ship Technology

resolution.text: Exports resumed through a corridor agreed under the Black Sea Grain Initiative, with the first departure from Odesa on 2022-08-01 and later movements at Chornomorsk and Pivdennyi. Mariupol stayed closed to commercial traffic.

events.title: Floods cut both rail lines and the highways serving the Port of Vancouver
events.severity_basis: Rail service to and from the port was halted from 2021-11-16 until 2021-11-23 (seven days) while trucks kept serving all four container terminals, so the nearest rubric match is a stoppage of 24 hours to seven days; a measured effect may justify a correction.
events.summary: Flooding and mudslides after an atmospheric river storm that began on 2021-11-14 (14 November 2021) damaged the railways and highways linking the Port of Vancouver to the rest of Canada. On 2021-11-16 the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority said all rail service to and from the port had stopped, because neither CN nor CP could run trains between Kamloops and Vancouver. Trucks kept serving all four container terminals, and demand for ship anchorages neared capacity. British Columbia declared a province-wide state of emergency effective 2021-11-17. Canadian Pacific reopened its line on 2021-11-23 (23 November 2021) and trains from both railways used it, while CN expected its own line to open on 2021-11-25.

timeline.text: An atmospheric river storm begins in British Columbia. Canadian Pacific later reports damage at 30 locations on its Thompson and Cascade subdivisions, 20 with significant loss of infrastructure.

The port authority says all rail service to and from the port is halted. CN and CP report that no trains can move between Kamloops and Vancouver, and flooding has also closed the main highway routes into the region.
A provincial state of emergency takes effect for all of British Columbia for an initial 14 days. The port authority says it has no timeline for resuming rail service.

The port authority reports trucks running normally at all four container terminals and anchorage demand nearing capacity across all vessel types. CP says rail lines could be restored by the middle of the following week.
Canadian Pacific announces it will reopen its line between Kamloops and Vancouver by midday on 2021-11-23.

CP runs two inspection trains and expects regular service to start later that day, with both CP and CN trains using the line under slow orders. CN moves its own line's estimated opening to 2021-11-25.
The port authority reports four trains crossed CP's line the previous day, with more CP and CN trains expected that day under low speed limits.

cause.text: The port authority attributed the disruption to widespread flooding in Metro Vancouver, the Fraser Valley and the British Columbia interior, which damaged rail and road infrastructure. Canadian Pacific attributed its damage to the atmospheric river storm that began on 2021-11-14.
cause.attributed_by: Vancouver Fraser Port Authority

resolution.text: Canadian Pacific reopened its Kamloops to Vancouver line and regular rail service started over it on 2021-11-23, carrying both railways' trains at reduced speed. CN expected to open its own line on 2021-11-25. The port authority warned that more rain was forecast and that closures could recur.
