events.title: Hurricane Ida closes New Orleans and the Lower Mississippi River
events.severity_basis: Port wide stoppage of 24 hours to seven days; vessel movement on the Lower Mississippi River was prohibited from 2021-08-28 and the river reopened to all traffic on 2021-09-03.
events.summary: From 2021-08-28 (28 August 2021) the Captain of the Port set port condition Zulu before Hurricane Ida and prohibited vessel movement on the Lower Mississippi River, closing the Port of New Orleans and the other river ports of southeast Louisiana. Ida made landfall in Louisiana on 2021-08-29 as a category 4 hurricane. A downed transmission tower dropped power lines across the channel near mile marker 106.5 and a survey of the ship channel was required before traffic could return. The Coast Guard reopened the river to all vessel traffic on 2021-09-03 (3 September 2021), with speed and tow size limits between mile markers 108 and 167.5. The port resumed limited cargo work on 2021-09-02 and container operations on 2021-09-07.

timeline.text: The Captain of the Port sets port condition Zulu. From 14:00 no vessel movement is authorised between mile marker 167.5 above Head of Passes and mile marker 20 below it, and from 22:00 the closure extends upriver to mile marker 303.
Hurricane Ida makes landfall in Louisiana as a category 4 storm, according to the Port of New Orleans, which reports that seven general cargo vessels stayed in port through the storm.
The port resumes limited cargo and vessel operations, starting with breakbulk work at the Louisiana Avenue complex.

The Coast Guard opens the Lower Mississippi River to all vessel traffic after power lines from a downed transmission tower are cleared and the ship channel is surveyed, keeping speed and tow size limits in place.
Container operations resume at the Napoleon Avenue Container Terminal, according to the port.

cause.text: The Coast Guard closed the river to vessel movement ahead of Hurricane Ida, which made landfall in Louisiana on 2021-08-29. Reopening waited on the removal of power lines from a transmission tower that fell across the waterway near mile marker 106.5 and on a survey of the ship channel.
cause.attributed_by: U.S. Coast Guard

resolution.text: The Coast Guard reopened the Lower Mississippi River to all vessel traffic on 2021-09-03 once obstructions were cleared and the channel surveyed. Port terminals restarted in stages, with limited cargo work from 2021-09-02 and container operations from 2021-09-07.

events.title: Meishan container terminal at Ningbo-Zhoushan closed for two weeks
events.severity_basis: A single terminal inside the port was closed for 14 days, which meets the criterion of a terminal closure over 72 hours.
events.summary: The Meishan Island International Container Terminal at Ningbo-Zhoushan stopped container gate and vessel work on 2021-08-11 (11 August 2021) after a terminal worker tested positive for COVID-19, and reopened on 2021-08-25 (25 August 2021). Trucking to and from the terminal was suspended, a nearby warehouse stopped work, and carriers moved calls to other Ningbo terminals including Beilun and Yongzhou or skipped the port to protect schedules. The rest of Ningbo-Zhoushan stayed open throughout. Trade press reported at the time that the shutdown risked repeating the congestion seen at Yantian in Shenzhen earlier in 2021, with about 140 container ships already waiting off Ningbo and Shanghai. Gate and berthing work resumed on 2021-08-25, with landside services restarting in stages.

timeline.text: The terminal stops container gate in and gate out work under local COVID-19 controls after a worker tests positive. Vessel operations at the terminal stop and trucking to the site is suspended.

Trade press reports that carriers in the Ocean Alliance are among the main users of the terminal and warns of congestion spreading, with about 140 container ships already waiting off Ningbo and Shanghai after Typhoon In-Fa.
Container gate in, gate out and vessel berthing resume at the terminal. Warehouse and other landside services restart in stages the same day.

cause.text: The terminal was locked down under COVID-19 controls imposed by the local authorities after a terminal worker tested positive, according to the carrier advisory tracking the closure.
cause.attributed_by: Maersk, citing local authorities

resolution.text: The terminal reopened on 2021-08-25 after 14 days, with gate and berthing work resuming and landside services restarting in stages. The rest of Ningbo-Zhoushan had stayed open throughout.

events.no_effect_note: Meishan is one terminal inside the Ningbo-Zhoushan port series. A closure at that level sits below the resolution of the port level series we publish, so no effect is measured for this record.

events.title: Typhoon In-fa halts container handling at Shanghai and Ningbo ports
events.severity_basis: Yangshan terminals halted operations on 2021-07-24 and trade press reported the Shanghai ports shut until at least 2021-07-27 with operations restarting that day, which falls in the band of 24 hours to 7 days at port level.
events.summary: Typhoon In-fa halted container handling at Shanghai and Ningbo in late July 2021. Lloyd's List reported on 2021-07-23 (23 July 2021) that pickups and deliveries were being suspended at terminals in both ports, and said Yangshan would stop box pickups from 06:00 and deliveries from 12:00 on 2021-07-24. On 2021-07-24 the Yangshan maritime safety administration said vessels had been moved out and all terminals had halted. In-fa reached Zhejiang province on 2021-07-25. Bloomberg reported Shanghai's ports shut until at least 2021-07-27, and Lloyd's List said on that date that operations were restarting. No source reviewed gives a reopening time for Ningbo or for individual Shanghai terminals.

timeline.text: Lloyd's List reports container pickups and deliveries suspended at terminals in Shanghai and Ningbo ahead of In-fa, with Yangshan due to stop pickups from 06:00 and deliveries from 12:00 local time on 2021-07-24.

All container ship docks at Yangshan are reported shut and about 150 vessels evacuated. The Yangshan Port Maritime Safety Administration says on social media that all terminals have halted operations.
In-fa reaches Zhejiang province. SEKO Logistics later reports container freight terminals at Shanghai and Ningbo shut and vessel movements delayed.
Bloomberg reports all of Shanghai's ports and some in neighbouring areas shut until at least 2021-07-27, including Yangshan, with oil, LNG and bulk cargo also stopped.
Lloyd's List reports port operations restarting and a backlog to clear, with about 10% of the usual container vessel berthings at key Chinese hubs in the past week.

cause.text: The ports halted ahead of and during Typhoon In-fa, which China's National Meteorological Centre placed under an orange alert and which crossed Zhejiang province on 2021-07-25.
cause.attributed_by: Lloyd's List, Bloomberg and the Yangshan Port Maritime Safety Administration, as reported

resolution.text: Lloyd's List reported port operations restarting on 2021-07-27. Container News described the Shanghai closure as lasting four days. The sources reviewed do not give a reopening time for Ningbo.

events.title: Cyberattack on Transnet disrupts South African container terminals
events.severity_basis: Container handling at four ports ran on manual systems for more than 72 hours, with force majeure in place from 2021-07-26 until it was uplifted with effect from 2021-08-02.
events.summary: A cyberattack on the South African state logistics company Transnet from 2021-07-22 (22 July 2021) disrupted the systems that run its container terminals. Transnet Port Terminals declared force majeure on 2021-07-26 at the container terminals in Durban, Cape Town, Ngqura and Port Elizabeth, where loading and discharge switched to manual processes and ran more slowly than normal. Transnet Port Terminals described the incident as "an act of cyber-attack, security intrusion and sabotage". The terminal operating system was restored in stages, and Transnet said the force majeure would be uplifted with effect from 2021-08-02 once it could meet its contractual obligations again. Transnet did not name an attacker. A cybersecurity firm reported that a ransom note left on Transnet systems matched a known ransomware family.

timeline.text: Transnet systems are disrupted by a cyberattack, affecting IT applications used across the company and the terminal operating system at its container terminals.
Transnet Port Terminals declares force majeure at the container terminals in Durban, Cape Town, Ngqura and Port Elizabeth, and moves container handling onto manual systems.
A cybersecurity firm reports that a ransom note left on Transnet computers is linked to a ransomware family known as Death Kitty, Hello Kitty and Five Hands. Transnet does not attribute the attack.
Transnet says operations have normalised after the terminal operating system was restored in stages and that the force majeure will be uplifted with effect from the following day.
The force majeure declared at the four container terminals is uplifted.

cause.text: Transnet Port Terminals said it had experienced "an act of cyber-attack, security intrusion and sabotage" that disrupted its normal processes. A cybersecurity firm reported that a ransom note found on Transnet systems was linked to a known ransomware family. Transnet did not publicly identify those responsible.
cause.attributed_by: Transnet Port Terminals, with the ransomware link attributed by the cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike

resolution.text: Transnet restored the terminal operating system in stages across the container terminals, said operations had normalised and uplifted the force majeure with effect from 2021-08-02.

events.title: COVID-19 controls cut container handling at Yantian in Shenzhen
events.severity_basis: Berths in use at the port fell from 20 to five and the western terminal area was closed from 2021-05-26 to 2021-06-24, a port level restriction lasting more than seven days.
events.summary: Container handling at Yantian in Shenzhen was cut from 2021-05-25 (25 May 2021), after COVID-19 cases were found in the port area, and full operations resumed on 2021-06-24 (24 June 2021). The terminal operator stopped taking laden export containers through the gate late on 2021-05-25, and from 2021-05-26 export and transhipment boxes in the western area were held and operations there stopped. Berths in use fell from 20 to five. Carriers reported the eastern berths running at about 30 percent of normal output in early June, recovering through the month, while about 90 ships skipped Yantian and Shekou. The operator said all berths, including the western area, returned to normal from 00:00 on 2021-06-24, with laden gate in raised to 9,000 trucks a day.

timeline.text: COVID-19 is reported at the port, the start of the outbreak that led to the restrictions, according to trade press.
The terminal suspends acceptance of laden export containers at the gate from late on 2021-05-25 through 2021-05-27, according to the carrier advisory.
Export and transhipment containers in the western area of the terminal are held and operations there stop until further notice. Yard density in the terminal is reported at 96 percent.
Trade press reports the eastern part of the terminal working at about 30 percent of normal output with the western area still shut, tens of thousands of TEU backed up and ships waiting off the port.
The carrier reports yard density down to 60 percent and about 90 ships, including partner services, having skipped Yantian and Shekou.

The operator says all berths, including the western area, resumed normal operations from 00:00, with laden gate in raised to 9,000 trucks a day and export boxes accepted seven days before vessel arrival.

cause.text: The operator attributed the reduced operations to COVID-19 control measures in the port area after cases were found there, and said on 2021-06-23 that the virus was under control and terminal capacity had recovered.
cause.attributed_by: Yantian International Container Terminals

resolution.text: All 20 berths, including those in the western area, returned to normal work from 00:00 on 2021-06-24, with gate throughput and container acceptance restored to normal levels. Backlogs and vessel schedule gaps persisted after that date.

events.title: Container ship X-Press Pearl burns and sinks off Colombo
events.severity_basis: No source records a stoppage of Port of Colombo operations; the loss was confined to one vessel and its cargo at the anchorage, with a local ban on shipping and fishing in the affected area.
organisations: Marine Environment Protection Authority of Sri Lanka
events.summary: A fire broke out aboard the container ship X-Press Pearl at the Colombo anchorage on 2021-05-20 (20 May 2021), about 9.5 miles off the Sri Lankan capital, and the vessel sank during a tow attempt on or about 2021-06-02 (2 June 2021). The ship was carrying 1,486 containers loaded in part at Hazira, India, including nitric acid and other chemicals. Firefighting involved the Sri Lanka Ports Authority, the Sri Lanka Navy and the Indian Coast Guard. The Sri Lanka Ports Authority reported on 2021-05-30 that the hull remained structurally intact. Salvors boarded on 2021-06-01, when the fire was reported out and the government ordered the ship towed to deeper water. Sri Lanka barred shipping and fishing in the affected area. No source records a suspension of Port of Colombo operations.

timeline.text: Fire breaks out in a deck container aboard the X-Press Pearl at the Colombo anchorage. The operator reports all 25 crew safe and the fire under control by 2021-05-24, with tugs cooling the vessel.

The Sri Lanka Ports Authority reports that firefighting tugs continue, that the hull remains structurally intact and that no oil or chemical spill has been observed, while salvors examine a tow connection.
Salvors board the vessel and the fire is confirmed extinguished. The government orders the ship moved to deep water away from the coast.
The vessel settles by the stern during the tow attempt and partially sinks about 9.5 miles off Colombo. Sri Lanka bans shipping and fishing in the affected area.

cause.text: The operator said early indications pointed to a chemical reaction in hazardous cargo carried in containers, and Sri Lankan authorities opened an investigation, including a court order requiring three of the ship's officers to remain in the country.
cause.attributed_by: X-Press Feeders and the Sri Lankan criminal investigation

resolution.text: The fire was reported out on 2021-06-01 and the vessel partially sank during the tow attempt on 2021-06-02, ending the firefighting response. Sri Lanka kept a ban on shipping and fishing in the affected area while salvage and shoreline clean up continued.

events.no_effect_note: The vessel burned and sank at the anchorage rather than at a berth. No cited source records a suspension or restriction of Port of Colombo operations, only a local ban on shipping and fishing in the affected area, so a change in the port's daily call series could not be attributed to this event.

events.title: Container ship Ever Given grounds and blocks the Suez Canal
events.severity_basis: Complete closure of a chokepoint for any duration; the Suez Canal was shut to transits from 2021-03-23 until 2021-03-29.
events.summary: On 2021-03-23 (23 March 2021) the container ship Ever Given grounded on the eastern bank of the Suez Canal at kilometre 151, in the southern section of the waterway, and came to rest across the channel. The vessel was fifth in a northbound convoy and was bound from China to Rotterdam, so the blockage sat on the Asia to North Europe route. Traffic stopped in both directions while the canal authority ran dredging and towing work. The ship was pulled clear on 2021-03-29 (29 March 2021) and taken to the Great Bitter Lake for inspection, and transits restarted the same day. The canal authority said the queue of 422 ships held by the closure finished transiting on 2021-04-03 (3 April 2021). The flag state investigation recorded no deaths or injuries.

timeline.text: The Ever Given grounds at kilometre 151 at about 07:40 local time, the flag state investigation later timing it at 07:41. The ship lies across the channel and stops northbound and southbound traffic.
The Suez Canal Authority reports that refloating work is continuing with dredgers and tugs and that navigation through the canal is suspended.
The canal authority attributes the grounding to winds of about 40 knots and a sandstorm that cut visibility.

The canal authority announces that the vessel has been refloated, with the stern moved away from the bank, and says navigation will resume once the ship is back on course. The vessel is taken to the Great Bitter Lake.
The canal authority says the last of the 422 ships held by the closure have completed their transits.

cause.text: The Suez Canal Authority attributed the grounding to winds of about 40 knots and a sandstorm that reduced visibility. The Panama Maritime Authority, as flag state, found the vessel held valid certificates and set out a combination of wind, bank and squat effects, speed and bridge team and pilotage decisions as the sequence leading to the grounding.
cause.attributed_by: Suez Canal Authority; Panama Maritime Authority

resolution.text: Salvage work refloated the ship and moved it to the Great Bitter Lake for inspection, and the canal reopened to traffic. The waiting queue was cleared by 2021-04-03.

events.title: Winter storm closes Houston, Galveston, Texas City and Corpus Christi ports
events.severity_basis: Port Houston suspended work at its eight public terminals for what a trade report described as nearly a week, and the Houston Ship Channel closed from 19:30 on 2021-02-16 to 10:30 on 2021-02-17, which falls in the band of 24 hours to 7 days at port level.
events.summary: A severe winter storm disrupted Texas Gulf Coast ports in February 2021. Galveston and Texas City closed to vessel traffic at 19:00 on 2021-02-14 (14 February 2021), and the Corpus Christi pilots stopped boarding ships that day. According to the Coast Guard as reported by Argus, the Port of Houston and Houston Ship Channel closed at 19:30 on 2021-02-16 and reopened at 10:30 on 2021-02-17. Port Houston suspended its eight public terminals for what a trade report called nearly a week, and told its commissioners on 2021-02-23 that all had resumed. The sources reviewed give no reopening time for Galveston, Texas City or Corpus Christi, and one trade report said no Coast Guard navigation restriction was posted on 2021-02-16.

timeline.text: Galveston and Texas City close to all vessel traffic at 19:00, and the Aransas-Corpus Christi Pilots Association stops boarding vessels in the Corpus Christi Ship Channel because of gale-force wind and record-low temperatures.

A Houston Pilots Association dispatcher says many terminals are closed, with about 13 vessels waiting to leave and 18 waiting to enter. The Maritime Executive reports no Captain of the Port restriction. That evening the Coast Guard closes the Houston Ship Channel and port at 19:30, and Corpus Christi closes at 23:50.

The Coast Guard reopens the Houston Ship Channel and Port of Houston at 10:30. Freeport closes at 07:45, and Galveston and Texas City remain closed. The Port of Corpus Christi says it is operating with limitations and that pilots are moving vessels sporadically.

At its regular meeting the Port of Houston Authority commission says the public terminals suspended during the storm have reopened, after a loss of power, water and other systems at several terminals.

cause.text: Port Houston said it suspended operations because of record sub-freezing temperatures, and the Port of Corpus Christi cited freezing temperatures, heavy precipitation, fog and gale-force wind. Port Houston said several public terminals also lost power and water.
cause.attributed_by: Port Houston and Port of Corpus Christi Authority

resolution.text: The Coast Guard reopened the Houston Ship Channel on 2021-02-17. Port Houston reported at its commission meeting on 2021-02-23 that all public terminals had resumed operations. The date is an upper bound, and the sources reviewed do not say when Galveston, Texas City, Freeport and Corpus Christi resumed. AJOT described the Port Houston shutdown as lasting nearly a week.

events.title: France closes its border to freight from the United Kingdom
events.severity_basis: Port wide stoppage of 24 hours to seven days, with the Port of Dover closed to accompanied traffic leaving the United Kingdom from the evening of 2020-12-20 until services resumed on 2020-12-23.
events.summary: On 2020-12-20 (20 December 2020) France barred arrivals from the United Kingdom over a coronavirus variant reported there, and the Port of Dover closed to accompanied traffic leaving the country. A French decree published the following day prohibited travel from the United Kingdom until midnight on 2020-12-23. Lorries queued in Kent, with 632 on the M20 and 2,188 at Manston airfield on 2020-12-22 according to figures reported that day. The United Kingdom and France agreed a protocol on 2020-12-22 under which sea, rail and air services resumed the next morning, with drivers required to show a negative test taken in the previous 72 hours. Queues at Dover took several more days to clear.

timeline.text: France stops accepting arrivals from the United Kingdom over a reported coronavirus variant. The Port of Dover closes to accompanied traffic leaving the country and Channel Tunnel services are suspended.

The two governments agree a protocol to reopen the border for accompanied freight and some passenger services. Lorry drivers must take a lateral flow test, and travellers must show a negative test taken within 72 hours.
Sea, rail and air services resume in the morning and testing of drivers begins in Kent. Reported figures that week put 632 lorries on the M20 and 2,188 at Manston airfield.
Queues at Dover clear slowly as testing continues, with military personnel deployed to carry out tests.

cause.text: The French government restricted movements from the United Kingdom because of the health situation there after a new coronavirus variant was reported, setting the prohibition out in a decree that ran until midnight on 2020-12-23. The United Kingdom Department for Transport then agreed a protocol with France to reopen the border with testing.

resolution.text: The border reopened to accompanied freight on 2020-12-23 under a protocol requiring a negative test, and ferry and tunnel services resumed that morning. Clearing the lorries held in Kent took several more days.

events.title: Container ship queue off Los Angeles and Long Beach
events.severity_basis: No closure criterion applies to a queueing episode and no measured effect is available at month precision, so Moderate is proposed for editor review.
events.summary: From October 2020 until 2022-11-22 (22 November 2022) container ships waited off San Pedro Bay for berths at the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach. The Marine Exchange of Southern California reported 60 vessels at anchor on 2021-01-28 and began holding ships in drift areas outside the anchorage for the first time since 2004. An industry working group of the exchange, the Pacific Maritime Association and the Pacific Merchant Shipping Association replaced arrival based queueing with places assigned on departure from the last port of call, effective 2021-11-16 (16 November 2021), and asked ships to wait outside a safety and air quality area extending 150 miles from the coast. The queue peaked at 109 container ships on 2022-01-09 and the exchange declared the backup over after 25 months.

timeline.text: A queue of container ships waiting for berths at Los Angeles and Long Beach begins to build, the start of the 25 month period later counted by the Marine Exchange of Southern California.
The Marine Exchange reports 60 vessels at anchor and places three ships in drift areas outside the anchorage, the first such use since 2004.

The new queueing process takes effect at Los Angeles and Long Beach. Ships are given a calculated time of arrival set when they leave their last port of call, and are asked to stay outside a safety and air quality area 150 miles from the coast.
The number of container ships waiting reaches its peak of 109.
The Marine Exchange count falls to 16 container ships, one at anchor and 15 outside the safety and air quality area.
The Marine Exchange reports no container ships waiting and declares the backup over after 25 months, with the agreement of both ports and the two industry associations.

cause.text: Trade reporting linked the queue to import volumes that outran berth, terminal and inland capacity from late 2020, and its end to falling volumes and to the queueing process that moved waiting ships far offshore. The sources cited do not give a single official cause.

resolution.text: The queue fell through 2022 as arriving ships slowed their Pacific crossings under the new queueing process and volumes declined. The Marine Exchange of Southern California declared the backup over on 2022-11-22 with the concurrence of both ports and the two industry associations.

events.no_effect_note: The start is known only to the month and the episode ran for 25 months, well beyond the effect window. A daily effect on container port calls is not computed; an editor may add explicit windows, for example around the 2022-01-09 peak, with a written reason.

events.title: Explosion at the Port of Beirut halts port operations
events.severity_basis: Port level disruption lasting more than seven days; the United Nations reported the port working at 30 per cent capacity with two quays and five of 16 cranes nine days after the explosion.
organisations: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
events.summary: An explosion at the Port of Beirut on 2020-08-04 (4 August 2020) destroyed much of the port and stopped operations at Lebanon's main maritime gateway. The blast followed the ignition of ammonium nitrate stored in a port warehouse. Container lines diverted vessels to Tripoli while the site was cleared. The container terminal, which sits away from the blast centre, restarted on 2020-08-10 (10 August 2020), and two carriers said their services to Beirut had resumed. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs reported on 2020-08-13 that two quays had reopened, that five of the port's 16 cranes were working and that the port was functioning at 30 per cent of capacity. A Lebanese judicial investigation into the explosion has been suspended repeatedly and no trial has taken place.

timeline.text: An explosion at the Port of Beirut destroys much of the port. Reporting attributes the blast to ammonium nitrate stored in a port warehouse.
The container terminal restarts. One carrier reports discharging its first container vessel that day and another says the terminal suffered limited damage and has resumed working.
Carriers resume bookings for Beirut after diverting vessels to Tripoli, and the port handles cargo again for merchants.
The United Nations reports two quays open, five of 16 cranes working, two more cranes due back by 2020-08-14, and the port at 30 per cent of capacity.
Questioning in the judicial investigation is suspended again after legal complaints seeking the removal of the investigating judge.
Six years after the explosion no trial has been held. The investigating judge sealed the case file in March 2026 and referred it to the Court of Cassation.

cause.text: Reporting attributes the explosion to the ignition of ammonium nitrate that had been stored at the port for years. The Lebanese judicial investigation has been suspended repeatedly by legal challenges brought by officials it sought to question, and no court has ruled on responsibility.
cause.attributed_by: Lebanese judicial investigation at the Court of Cassation

resolution.text: Container operations restarted on 2020-08-10 once storage areas were cleared, and carriers resumed calls at Beirut over the following days. The port was still working at reduced capacity on 2020-08-13, with two quays and five of 16 cranes in service.

events.title: Vehicle carrier Golden Ray capsizes and blocks the Brunswick channel
events.severity_basis: Port wide stoppage of 24 hours to seven days; the Port of Brunswick was closed to commercial traffic from 2019-09-08 until transits resumed on a case by case basis on 2019-09-11, with one way transits until 2019-11-14.
events.summary: On 2019-09-08 (8 September 2019) the vehicle carrier Golden Ray capsized in St. Simons Sound shortly after leaving the Port of Brunswick, Georgia, with a fire on board, closing the sound and the port to commercial traffic. The Coast Guard reported that all 24 people on board were rescued, four of them after being trapped in the hull, and set a safety zone half a mile around the wreck. Two cargo ships were allowed to leave under monitored transit late on 2019-09-11, and the port reopened on a case by case basis, with cargo that could be diverted sent to Savannah and Charleston. The channel stayed limited to one way traffic while salvage continued, and round the clock commercial transits resumed on 2019-11-14 (14 November 2019).

timeline.text: The 656 foot vehicle carrier capsizes in St. Simons Sound at about 02:00 with a fire on board. The Coast Guard rescues 20 people, four crew members remain trapped, and the Captain of the Port sets a safety zone half a mile around the vessel.
The four trapped crew members are rescued after nearly 40 hours in the hull, according to the safety board, bringing all 24 people on board to safety.
Two cargo vessels leave the port under monitored transit past the wreck, the first movements since the capsizing.

The port reopens on a case by case basis, with priority for perishable cargo and other vessels diverted to Savannah and Charleston while the unified command studies how passing ships affect the wreck.
The unified command and the Georgia Ports Authority restore round the clock commercial transits, with vessels still passing the wreck one at a time.
The safety board publishes its report, finding that an error in entering ballast quantities into the stability program left the ship with too little righting arm during an outbound turn.

cause.text: The National Transportation Safety Board determined that the probable cause was an officer's error in entering ballast quantities into the ship's stability calculation program, which led to an incorrect stability assessment and left the vessel without enough righting arm during a turn outbound from Brunswick. The operator's failure to verify stability calculations contributed.
cause.attributed_by: National Transportation Safety Board

resolution.text: Transits past the wreck resumed on a case by case basis from 2019-09-11 and the Port of Brunswick returned to round the clock commercial traffic on 2019-11-14, with vessels passing one at a time while the Golden Ray was dismantled in place.

events.title: Iran seizes the tanker Stena Impero in the Strait of Hormuz
events.severity_basis: A restriction at a chokepoint; after the seizure the United Kingdom raised the security level for British flagged shipping to level 3 and advised against all passage through the Strait of Hormuz.
events.summary: On 2019-07-19 (19 July 2019) Iranian forces boarded and seized the British flagged product tanker Stena Impero as it passed through the Strait of Hormuz, and took the ship to Bandar Abbas with its 23 crew aboard. The United Kingdom government said the vessel was intercepted in the westbound traffic lane inside Omani territorial waters by fast boats and a helicopter of the Revolutionary Guard, and called the seizure a breach of international law. Iran said the ship had committed marine violations. On 2019-07-22 (22 July 2019) the Department for Transport raised the security level for British flagged shipping to level 3 and advised against all passage through the strait. Seven crew were released in early September, and the ship left Bandar Abbas for Dubai on 2019-09-27 (27 September 2019).

timeline.text: Iranian forces board the Stena Impero in the Strait of Hormuz at about 16:00 United Kingdom time and take her towards Iran. The operator reports losing contact with the ship.

The Foreign Secretary tells Parliament that the Department for Transport has raised the security level for British flagged shipping to level 3, advising against all passage in Iranian waters and in the strait as a whole.
The operator says seven of the crew are to be released, and reports on the following day that they have left the vessel.
The vessel leaves Bandar Abbas and sails for Dubai, where the remaining crew disembark for medical checks.

cause.attributed_by: Government of Iran; United Kingdom government

resolution.text: Iran released the ship after about ten weeks. The operator said the vessel had left Iranian waters and reached Dubai, where the crew disembarked.
